Three Rivers Messages Handbook

For front desk, Billing, providers and admins

How Messages works, from a patient's first message to Archive.

Messages brings the practice's email, texts, calls, voicemails and faxes into the dashboard, grouped by patient. This handbook covers what each person sees, how to reply, match, hand off and archive, and the settings admins look after.

Chapter 01 of 16 · Start here

Messages at a glance

What feeds Messages, who sees what, and what never leaves Gmail or Spruce.

What Messages is

Messages is a page in the dashboard, in the left sidebar with the inbox icon. It shows the practice's correspondence in one place:

  • email in the practice Gmail mailboxes an admin has connected;
  • texts, calls, missed calls, voicemails and faxes on the Spruce lines an admin has turned on.

Messages groups everything by patient. When a conversation belongs to a Healthie patient, it shows under that patient, so one row holds their email and their texts together. Conversations that don't belong to a patient yet show on their own.

Gmail and Spruce stay as they are

Messages reads from Gmail and Spruce and sends through them; it doesn't replace either one.

  • Replies you send from Messages go out through the same mailbox or Spruce line, and they show in Gmail or Spruce too.
  • Handled by, internal notes and who has read what live only in Messages.
  • Archive stays in Messages too, until an admin turns on Archive in Spruce and Gmail in Settings › Inboxes. From then on, archiving here archives the conversation in Spruce and takes the email out of the Gmail inbox (nothing is deleted), and archiving there archives it here. See Archive, waiting and unread.
  • Messages keeps only the sender, subject and a short preview for the list. The full text is read fresh from Gmail and Spruce each time you open a patient.

Who sees what

What you see depends on your role. An admin sets each person up in Settings › Messages access.

Sees Can also
Admin Every patient, and conversations not linked to anyone Everything, including the settings
Front desk Every patient, email included, and Needs matching Choose who handles a patient, link conversations to patients
Billing Only patients handed to Billing, with their email Hand a patient back to front desk
Provider Only patients handed to them, without email unless an admin adds it Hand a patient back to front desk

Front desk sees every patient and decides who handles each one. Billing and providers see a patient only after front desk hands it to them. Billing and providers has more on their side of it.

Getting in

Admins can always open Messages. Everyone else needs three things: one role on their dashboard account (staff or provider), the Messages switch turned on for staff, and their own setup in Settings › Messages access. If one is missing, the page says which:

  • Messages is not open to staff yet. The switch is off. Providers see this too.
  • An admin needs to set up your Messages access.
  • An admin needs to choose your team in Messages access.
  • Your account needs exactly one of the staff and provider groups.

With Demo Mode on, Messages hides itself, because it holds real patient correspondence.

Keeping it private

  • Internal notes are for the team. Patients never see them.
  • The dashboard signs you out after 30 minutes without activity, after a one-minute Still there? warning. Anything you haven't sent is lost, so send or copy it first.
  • If your access changes while you're working (an admin changes your setup, or a patient is handed to someone else), the page lets go of what you can no longer see and starts over.

Chapter 02 of 16 · Start here

The list

Patient rows and loose conversations, the filters, the chips, archiving from the list, and search.

Two kinds of row

  • A patient row stands for everything linked to one Healthie patient: their email threads, their Spruce conversations, or both. When they have more than one conversation, a small number after the name says how many.
  • A conversation row is a conversation not linked to anyone yet: a new sender, a pharmacy, a vendor, a fax. This handbook calls these loose conversations.

A conversation linked to a patient never shows as its own row. You find it inside the patient.

What a row shows

  • The name. For a patient this comes from Healthie. For a loose conversation it's the sender, or Unknown number for a text from a number with no name.
  • The time of the latest activity: the time today, the date this year (Oct 21), or the full date for older ones.
  • A preview of the newest conversation. You: in front means the practice wrote last.
  • Chips:
  • the kind: Email, Text, Fax, Call, Missed call or Voicemail. Missed calls and voicemails are orange, because someone needs a call back.
  • Waiting 25m, Waiting 3h 59m and so on: how long someone has been waiting on the practice. See Archive, waiting and unread.
  • Archived: nothing is open.
  • Chart save to check: a file saved to the chart needs a look (see Save to chart).
  • Choose who handles: the patient's conversations were assigned to different people before, and someone should pick one owner.
  • @ Tagged: someone tagged you on this patient in a note. Hover over it to see who and when (see Tagging a teammate).
  • Initials in a circle: the person handling this patient, when it's someone by name.
  • A small warning triangle: Spruce or Gmail is out of step with a conversation here. Open the row to see what happened (see Chips about Spruce and Gmail).
  • On a loose conversation, a match chip: Which patient? or No patient in amber, Not a patient in gray. A conversation whose messages are linked one at a time says why instead: Shared number, Shared address, Fax: link each one or Link each message, with how many are linked so far.

A blue dot and bold text mean unread for you. Unread is per person: your reading doesn't clear the dot for anyone else.

Tabs and filters

Inbox holds everything open. Front desk and admins also have Needs matching, with a count of conversations waiting for a patient (see Needs matching).

The chips narrow the Inbox:

  • All
  • Waiting: someone is waiting on the practice.
  • Mine: patients handled by you by name, and loose conversations assigned to you. Billing holds patients as a team, so Mine stays empty for Billing staff.
  • Tagged: patients you're tagged on. It shows only once someone has tagged you. For front desk it lists tagged patients even after they're archived.
  • Email, Texts, Voicemail (missed calls included), Fax: by channel. A chip with nothing in it hides itself.
  • Archived: patients and conversations with nothing open. It pages back with Load older.

Each chip except Archived shows a count. A + after a count means there are more than the page could count.

The list refreshes itself every 30 seconds. On the Inbox, the round arrow refreshes it now. When there are more rows, Load more sits at the bottom.

Archiving from the list

You don't have to open a row to archive it. Point at a row, or reach it with the Tab key, and two controls appear on it: a checkbox over the avatar and an Archive button at the end of the row (its tooltip says Archive messages).

  • Archive on a row archives it straight away, the same as opening the patient and pressing Archive. Anything newer than what the row showed stays in the Inbox, and the message says why.
  • The checkbox selects the row. Shift-click another row's checkbox to select every row in between. While anything is selected, a bar above the list says how many, with Archive and Clear, and a box to select every row on the page.
  • Archive on the bar archives the selection, up to 50 at a time. The message counts them, for example Archived 7. 2 stayed in the Inbox: new messages arrived. The ones that stayed are still selected, so you can open them and read what came in.
  • Changing the filter, the search or the tab clears the selection.

A row you can only reach because someone tagged you has no checkbox and no Archive: whoever handles the patient archives it. Billing and providers can archive their own patients from the list.

Some rows can't be archived from the list, so nothing gets cleared before someone has read it: a patient handed back to front desk with a note, a patient just handed to you that you haven't dealt with yet, a save to the chart that needs checking, and a patient with more than 50 conversations. Their button says Open the patient to archive and opens the patient instead.

One archive from the list runs at a time. While it runs, the other rows' Archive buttons wait.

Search

The search box finds rows by the patient's name or email as Healthie has them, and by sender and subject. Names need at least three letters. It doesn't search message text.

If many patients share the name, the list says Many patients match that name. Keep typing to narrow it. If Healthie can't be reached, it says Name search isn't working right now. Sender and subject still are.

Chapter 03 of 16 · Working a patient

A patient's timeline

Everything with one patient in one place: email, texts, calls, voicemails, notes and files.

The patient card

Open a patient row and their timeline fills the right side, starting at the newest message. The patient card stays at the top while you scroll, so you always see who this is:

  • name, with Discharged for an inactive patient;
  • Born, phone and email. On a narrow window this line is cut short; point at it to see all of it.

Under the name is a band with Group and Next visit (date, type and provider, or None booked). For front desk and admins it starts with Handled by (see Handled by and hand-offs).

On the right are Details, Open chart, Archive and, for Billing and providers, Hand back. Details opens more from Healthie: address, any balance due, insurance and eligibility, and the latest appointments. Providers don't get it. Open chart opens their chart in Healthie in a new tab.

Call is in the reply bar at the bottom, next to Text and Internal note, so it's always in reach (see Calling a patient).

One timeline for every channel

Everything with the patient sits in one list, oldest at the top, newest at the bottom:

  • email messages;
  • texts, drawn as chat bubbles, the patient's on the left and the practice's on the right;
  • calls, missed calls and voicemails;
  • internal notes, labeled Staff only;
  • hand-off and hand-back notes, in violet.

A day line (Today, Yesterday, or the date) marks each new day. Items from the same conversation sit together under a source line, such as Email · Question about my refill or Spruce · (857) 555-0101, with a Waiting or Archived chip.

In an email thread, the newest message is open and older ones are one line each. Click one to read it. A message sent from Messages says sent from the hub by and the name of whoever sent it.

Calls and voicemails

A call shows as Incoming call with its length, Outgoing call, Missed call or Voicemail. Missed calls and voicemails are orange: someone needs a call back. A voicemail shows Spruce's transcript in quotes, or Transcript in progress. or No speech in this voicemail. The recording is attached and plays in the preview.

An answered call is a record of a conversation that already happened. It never makes anyone wait.

Calling a patient

Call, in the reply bar at the bottom of the patient, calls the patient from your own phone, and they see the practice number, not yours. Your phone is the mobile on your entry on the People page, the person your dashboard login is linked to.

  1. Press Call. Call this patient? says what happens next. Press Set up call.
  2. Messages shows Dial now from your phone and a number to dial.
  3. From your phone, the one ending in the four digits shown, dial that number straight away. Spruce connects you to the patient.

It always calls the patient's number in Healthie; you can't type a different one. If nothing connects, close the box and set the call up again. Between 9pm and 8am the box warns that a call can wake people up.

If the call can't be set up, the box says why:

  • Your login is not linked to a person yet. An admin links your login to you on the Users page.
  • Your mobile is not on the People page yet. An admin adds it to your entry on People.
  • Your mobile is also on someone else on the People page. Each person needs their own mobile; an admin fixes it on People.
  • You are marked inactive on the People page, or your login is linked to two people. An admin fixes it on People or Users.
  • Calls are not set up yet. An admin chooses the line calls go out from in Settings › Inboxes.
  • Healthie has no phone number for this patient. Add one in Healthie first.
  • Spruce did not set up the call. Nothing rang. Try again, or call from Spruce.
  • Spruce did not confirm the call in time. Set it up again, and dial only the new number it gives you.

If you haven't dialed within two minutes, the box suggests setting the call up again.

Files

Attachments show as tiles with the file name, and the size for email attachments or the kind of file for Spruce ones. PDFs, images and audio open in a preview with a Download button; other files download straight away. Each time you open a file, Messages makes a short-lived copy for you, and that link stops working after a minute. Open the file again if you need it later.

Staff can save a file to the patient's chart with the button beside the tile. Save to chart covers it.

A fax, or a message from a shared number or address, shows in a patient's timeline once it is linked to them on its own (see Needs matching). Its line says so, for example Fax · linked on its own or Text · from a shared number, and only that message shows, never the rest of its conversation.

An email from a shared address, or one in a conversation that moved to this patient, shows to Billing, providers and anyone tagged as who it is from and when only: its text, subject and attachments are hidden from them until front desk shows it to them. The email says Only front desk can see this email’s text. They can show it to you if you need it. and its subject shows as Subject hidden. Front desk and admins read it whole, with Billing and providers who see this patient see only that this email is here. and Show its text to the patient's team under it. What is hidden and why is in Mixed conversations.

Long histories

The timeline loads a patient's five most recent conversations. Load 2 older conversations (or however many there are) fetches the next ones.

Banners above the timeline tell you when something is off:

  • One conversation has new activity since this opened. Press Refresh to see it.
  • A conversation that couldn't be read says why: it's no longer in Gmail or Spruce, its mailbox needs reconnecting in Settings › Inboxes, or it could not be loaded right now. It ends Archive leaves it open.
  • Email about this patient stays with front desk and billing. You don't have email access, so their email isn't shown.

Chapter 04 of 16 · Working a patient

Replying and notes

Email replies, texts, quiet hours, internal notes, and what happens to a draft.

Where your reply goes

You reply in one conversation at a time. Messages picks the conversation the patient last wrote in. When the patient has more than one, Reply in at the bottom lets you choose: an email thread by its subject, a Spruce conversation by its number, or New email… to start a new thread (see New email). If you change Reply in with something typed, Messages asks before throwing it away.

A reply always goes out the way the conversation came in. An email reply goes from the conversation's own mailbox, and a text goes from the Spruce line the patient used.

Texting

Press Text. The box shows who it goes to and a character count out of 1,600. The footer says which line it Sends from.

  • Send sends it now. Send and archive sends it and archives that conversation.
  • After sending, a card under the timeline shows Sending…, then Sent to Spruce. It will appear above in a moment. "Sent" means Spruce accepted it. Spruce doesn't report delivery.
  • Fax lines can't be answered here: the page says Faxes are answered in Spruce.
  • A text linked to this patient on its own (from a shared number, see Needs matching) goes to that shared number. The box says Text to a shared number and Shared number: more than one patient may read texts sent here. This text is about this patient and is kept on their timeline only. It answers that message only; once Spruce has it, it shows in this patient's timeline and no one else's.

Quiet hours

From 9pm to 8am Eastern, a text can wake someone up. During those hours the text box shows It's quiet hours (9pm to 8am). Texts now can wake people up. and two buttons:

  • Send at 8:00 AM has Spruce send it at 8am. The card says Spruce will send this at 8:00 AM. You can cancel it in Spruce before then. The patient counts as answered only once Spruce shows it sent that text. If it was cancelled in Spruce, or Spruce never shows it went, the card turns to Not confirmed a few minutes after 8am and the patient stays Waiting: check the conversation in Spruce. If Spruce no longer lists it but a text went out at 8am, the card says Sent or cancelled: check Spruce. The patient still shows as Waiting until someone replies or archives.
  • Send now sends it straight away.

The 8am time is shown in your computer's time zone. Send and archive isn't offered during quiet hours, so archive the patient separately.

If Messages can't check its Spruce lines for a moment, the page says Texts are temporarily unavailable and texts are left out until it can. Nothing is lost: a text you were writing stays in the box (sending is off and says why), and it comes back on its own. Archive and Hand back are off until then, so nothing is archived with a text you couldn't see.

A reply answers what was on your screen when you sent it. If the patient wrote again while you were typing (a text overnight, before an 8am reply, too), the patient stays Waiting so someone reads the new message.

Replying by email

Choose an email conversation under Reply in. The strip offers Reply, Reply all (when others were on the email), Forward and Internal note.

  • To and Cc hold addresses as chips. Type an address and press Enter; Backspace removes the last one. A bad address turns red.
  • The footer says which mailbox it Sends from. You can't change it.
  • Forward sends on the newest email as it was when you pressed Forward, with its attachments, and you can add a note above it. The line under the box names that email. If a newer one arrives before you press Send, the line says so and the forward still sends the one you looked at; Forward the newest instead switches to the new one. You can't attach new files from Messages. Very large attachments (over 20 MB together) have to be forwarded from Gmail.
  • Send, or Send and archive to archive the conversation once Gmail accepts the email.

The reply shows as a card under the thread until Gmail syncs it into the timeline: Sent. It will appear above once Gmail syncs.

Messages not shown yet

Messages shows an email or text only once it has worked out who it belongs to, which happens as it syncs, usually within a minute. Until then the conversation says 1 email in this thread isn't shown yet. It will appear once checked, or open the thread in Gmail. (for a text, open the conversation in Spruce), and the message, its attachments and its sender don't appear anywhere. Opening the conversation asks Messages to check it, which also picks up older mail it never had (sent before the mailbox was connected, or moved out of Spam).

When someone new writes into a patient's email thread, Messages looks their address up in Healthie first. If it belongs to another patient, the conversation goes to Needs matching instead of staying on this patient. If Healthie doesn't know the address, the email shows here, but Messages doesn't treat that address as the patient's, so that person's own new emails aren't linked to the patient on their own.

When the sender's name shows another address

If an email's sender name looks like a different address from the one it came from, the email says The sender's name shows a different address from the one this came from, with the real address. Check who wrote before replying. Messages doesn't link such a sender to a patient on its own (see Needs matching).

When a send isn't confirmed

Sometimes Gmail or Spruce takes the message but doesn't answer in time. The card then says Not confirmed, for example Gmail hasn't confirmed this reply. It will appear above within a few minutes if it went out.

Don't send it again straight away. Wait a few minutes and look: at the timeline, the mailbox's Sent folder, or the conversation in Spruce. Messages never retries a send on its own, so nothing goes out twice unless you send it twice. Failed. Nothing was sent. means it definitely didn't go, and you can send again.

An email linked on its own (from a shared address) is answered the same way: the reply goes in its thread, in reply to that email, and the box says Shared address. If you're in Billing, a provider or tagged on the patient, your reply goes only to people already on that email, and while its text is hidden from you only to whoever sent it; the box says This email is linked to this patient on its own, so a reply goes only to people already on it. If you can't see who an email went to and there is nobody to reply to (an email the practice sent), the box says You can’t see whom this email went to, so you can’t reply to it here. Ask front desk to reply. Front desk can copy in someone new. Forward on such an email, from Billing, a provider or someone tagged, sends only what their timeline shows of it: a hidden text stays out (the forward says so), and so do its attachments and whom it went to, and a hidden subject becomes Fwd: message. Front desk and admins forward the whole email.

Internal notes

Internal note writes a note for the team on this conversation. It's never sent, and patients never see it.

Anyone who can open the conversation sees its notes, including a provider it's handed to. Notes stay in Messages; they don't appear in Gmail or Spruce. Press Save note.

Tagging a teammate

Front desk and admins can tag someone in an internal note, to ask them to look at a patient. Tagging works on a conversation linked to a patient, in the patient's timeline or in the conversation on its own.

  1. Press Internal note and start writing.
  2. Type @ and the start of a name. A list of people opens under the box, providers first. Pick someone with the arrow keys and Enter, or click them. Escape closes the list.
  3. Their name goes into the note as @Name, and a chip under the box says Tagging: and their name. Keep writing, then press Save note.

The chip also says if the person:

  • no Slack, sees it in Messages only: no Slack message can reach them, so they find out when they next open Messages.
  • can't see email, sees your note: on an email conversation, someone without email access sees your note but never the email.

You can tag up to five people in one note, but not yourself. To take someone off before saving, press the × on their chip, which also takes their @Name out of the text, or delete their @Name yourself.

When the note is saved, the page says Note saved. Tagged and the names, with a line for anyone the Slack message didn't reach. In the note, each tagged name is highlighted and Tagged: lists who.

Each person you tag:

  • gets a Slack message, if Slack can reach them, saying who tagged them, with a link to the patient. It never names the patient or repeats your note.
  • sees the patient on their list with a Tagged chip and your note on top, until they press Clear. They can read, reply, write notes and call. The rest stays with whoever handles the patient (see Billing and providers).

A tag doesn't change who handles the patient; to hand the patient over, use Handled by (see Handing off). Front desk and admins see who's tagged on a patient in the Handled by band (see Who handles a patient). Tagging someone again moves their tag to the newer note. If the conversation is later linked to another patient, the tag stops counting.

While Messages isn't open to staff, a tag on anyone but an admin is saved but does nothing until it's turned on, and no Slack message goes out.

Drafts

A reply you're writing lives only on the page, never in your browser's storage.

A draft belongs to the patient you started it for. If a teammate moves the conversation to another patient (or links a conversation that had no patient) while you write, Send and Save note stop and say This conversation's patient changed while you were writing. Nothing was sent, and your draft is still here. Check that the draft still makes sense for where the conversation is now, then press Send again. If the conversation left the patient you're viewing, sending is off and the composer says why.

  • Messages asks Discard your draft? before you pick another row, go back to the list, archive the patient, change Reply in, or go to another page from the sidebar. Keep editing keeps it.
  • Reloading or closing the tab gets your browser's own warning about leaving the page.
  • It's lost without asking if you're signed out after 30 minutes idle, or your access changes while you're writing. That's on purpose: nothing stays on screen after a sign-out.

The trash icon, Discard draft, throws the draft away without asking.

Chapter 05 of 16 · Working a patient

New email

Starting a new email thread with a patient, and what to do when Gmail doesn't confirm it.

Starting a new thread

To email a patient about something new, open the patient and choose New email… under Reply in. A new email starts its own thread and is filed under this patient straight away. Automatic matching never moves it.

  • From: a connected practice mailbox. If there are several, pick one.
  • To: only addresses this patient is known by: their email in Healthie, and any outside address that has written in on one of their email conversations. You can't type a new address here. To starts on the patient's email in Healthie. Every other address says where it came from, wrote in and the date, and choosing one shows Not the patient’s email in Healthie. If the patient has no email in Healthie, nothing is chosen for you: pick the address yourself (Choose who this goes to.). If Messages couldn't read the patient from Healthie just then, it says Couldn’t read the patient’s email from Healthie; choose an address.
  • Subject: one line.

Press Send. The page says Email sent, or Email sent. It shows here once it is filed under the patient.

New email is for people with email access: admins, front desk, Billing, and providers an admin has given email. It only works for a patient who already has a conversation in Messages.

When it can't send

Sending stays off, with the reason, when:

  • the chosen mailbox is no longer connected (choose another, or ask an admin to reconnect it);
  • no mailbox is connected at all;
  • no address is chosen yet (the patient has no email in Healthie);
  • the address is no longer known for this patient;
  • This patient has no email address on file.

When Gmail doesn't confirm it

If Gmail doesn't answer in time, the draft locks: We couldn’t confirm Gmail sent this. If it went, it shows here after the next sync. This draft can’t be sent again; discard it to write a new one.

Under the timeline, a reminder says We couldn’t confirm a new email to the address went. Messages keeps checking for a day. After that it says the email is no longer checked automatically. Look in Gmail before writing again.

Look in the mailbox's Sent folder in Gmail. If it went, it will show up on the patient. If it didn't, discard the draft and write it again. I’ve checked, dismiss clears the reminder; it doesn't change anything in Gmail.

Chapter 06 of 16 · Working a patient

Archive, waiting and unread

When a patient counts as waiting, what Archive closes, Archive in Spruce and Gmail, and what brings a patient back.

Waiting

A conversation is waiting when someone reached out and the practice hasn't answered yet. The Waiting chip on a row counts from when the oldest unanswered message arrived.

These start a wait:

  • an email from outside the practice;
  • a text, missed call, voicemail or fax from the patient.

These answer it:

  • an email reply to someone who wrote in, whether sent from Messages or straight from Gmail;
  • a text you send the patient from Messages;
  • a text someone types in the Spruce app;
  • a fax sent from Spruce;
  • Archive.

If the patient writes again while your reply is being sent, the conversation stays waiting. Answer the new message, or archive it.

These don't answer it:

  • Spruce's automatic reply ("Thank you for your message…");
  • the practice's automated texts, like booking links and reminders, and bulk texts;
  • a text set for 8:00 AM, until Spruce sends it. If someone cancels it in Spruce, it never counts;
  • an internal note, a phone call you made, or forwarding an email to a colleague.

These still show in the timeline. An automatic reply never takes the place of what the patient wrote in the list. If you called the patient back, archive them.

Archive

Archive sits at the top of the patient. It closes every conversation of theirs that you have access to, including older ones not loaded on screen, as long as nothing new arrived in them. Then it returns you to the list with Archived, or Archived (3 conversations) when there were several.

Archive won't close a conversation that changed after you opened the patient. When that happens, the message says what's still open and why, for example 1 archived. 1 still in the Inbox: new messages arrived. Have a look, then archive again. Other reasons:

  • a new conversation was added
  • moved to another patient
  • the contact reaches more than one patient
  • couldn't be loaded
  • someone changed who handles the patient

Read what came in, then press Archive again.

You can also archive straight from the list, one row or several at once. See Archiving from the list.

Archive doesn't change who handles the patient. The kanban's archive, which discharges a patient in Healthie, is a different thing: Archive in Messages only files the messages.

Archive in Spruce and Gmail

Once an admin turns it on in Settings › Inboxes (see Settings › Inboxes), Archive follows into Spruce and Gmail, and back:

  • Archiving in Messages archives the conversation in Spruce, or takes the email thread out of the Gmail inbox, within a minute or two. Gmail only loses the Inbox label; nothing is ever deleted.
  • Move to Inbox on a conversation, or a new message from the patient, brings it back to the inbox there too.
  • Archiving a conversation in the Spruce app or in Gmail archives it here. Moving it back to the inbox there brings it back here. In Gmail, anything that takes a thread out of the inbox counts, such as archiving or snoozing it. Moving a thread to Trash doesn't: Messages leaves the conversation as it was.
  • A hand-back archives what it closes there too.

If Spruce or Gmail is archived while the patient's newest message is still unread here, Messages keeps the conversation open and says Archived in Spruce. A newer message keeps it open here. (or Gmail). Read it, then archive it here.

Until an admin turns it on, Archive stays in Messages only and Spruce and Gmail are left as they are.

What brings a patient back

An archived patient comes back to the Inbox when:

  • the patient (or anyone outside) writes or texts again, or leaves a missed call or voicemail;
  • for front desk, Billing or a provider hands them back;
  • for Billing or a provider, front desk hands them over;
  • for front desk and admins, a file saved to the chart needs checking;
  • once Archive follows into Spruce and Gmail, someone moves the conversation back to the inbox there.

Your own replies never reopen a patient. There's no button to move a whole patient back to the Inbox; something new happening does it.

Unread

Opening a patient marks what you read as read, for you only. A patient timeline has no way to mark it unread again.

A loose conversation (not linked to a patient) works a little differently. At the top it has its own Archive and Move to Inbox, Mark unread, and an Assigned to menu for front desk to give it to someone.

The Archived list

The Archived chip lists patients and conversations with nothing open, newest first. Load older goes further back. Search works there too.

Chapter 07 of 16 · Routing

Needs matching

How conversations find their patient, linking one by hand, and Not a patient.

How a conversation finds its patient

Messages tries to link each new conversation to a Healthie patient on its own:

  • By a decision someone made before. If staff linked this sender to a patient earlier, their new conversations go straight to that patient: Linked automatically: staff linked this sender before. A sender marked Not a patient stays that way.
  • Email, by the exact address. One patient with that address: linked, Matched by email address. Several: Which patient?. None: No patient.
  • Texts and calls, by the phone number on the patient's file: Matched by phone number, Which patient? when the number belongs to more than one patient, or No patient when it belongs to nobody.

Automatic matching never overrides a link or a Not a patient that someone set by hand.

Messages also takes an automatic match back to you when its evidence changes:

  • A number that moves. When the number that matched a conversation is now on someone else's chart in Healthie, or on no chart at all any more, the conversation goes back to Which patient? with This number is no longer only on the linked patient's chart in Healthie, so its messages wait here. New texts wait there until you pick. A link you made yourself stays, with a warning: Number changed in Healthie beside the conversation, and on its patient panel This number is no longer only on this patient's chart in Healthie. Check this conversation still belongs here.
  • A number on two charts. When Healthie lists the same number for two patients (a parent's phone), it becomes a shared number (see below), and links on it are undone, yours included, kept as the hint. If that was a mistake fixed in Healthie (or a number in the middle of moving), once the number is back on one chart the shared mark goes, and the links you made come back on their own. If the number is now someone else's, your link comes back with the Number changed in Healthie warning, so check it. Automatic matches stay in Which patient?. A contact you marked shared yourself stays shared.
  • A sender name that shows another address. When an email's sender name looks like a different address from the one it came from, Messages doesn't link it on its own. The panel says The sender's name shows a different address from the one the email came from, so it was not matched automatically. Check who wrote, then pick.

The Needs matching tab

Front desk and admins have a Needs matching tab next to Inbox, with a count. It lists open conversations Messages couldn't link to one patient: the No patient and Which patient? ones, fax lines, and shared numbers and addresses. Link each sender once, and their later messages go straight to the patient. Faxes and shared contacts are linked one message at a time (below).

Open a conversation to see its patient panel. It says what Messages found, for example Which patient? and 2 patients use this address. Pick the one this is about.

Linking a conversation

Press Link a patient (or Pick one when Messages has candidates). Search Healthie by name or email, at least two letters. Patients Messages suggests show their name, date of birth and group; search results show name, email and group. Details opens the record without linking, so you can check the date of birth; Link links them.

The page says Patient linked. Later messages from this sender go straight to them. The link is saved for everyone, and the conversation now shows under the patient.

If a teammate linked or unlinked the conversation while your picker was open, yours is refused with Someone changed this conversation's patient meanwhile. Reload it and try again. Their decision stands; the panel shows it.

Not a patient

For a vendor, a newsletter or anyone who isn't a patient, press Not a patient (or This is not a patient in the search box). Their later messages skip Needs matching and show in the Inbox with a gray Not a patient chip. Linking any of their conversations to a patient later undoes it.

A fax line, a shared number or address, or an email with more than five people has no Not a patient: their later messages would skip Needs matching for good, and you couldn't undo it there. Archive the conversation instead (below).

Changing or undoing a link

Change patient in the conversation's patient panel moves it to another patient, or marks it not a patient. The patient timeline doesn't have this button. You'll see it on the conversation right after linking it.

Where the new patient's messages start

When you move a conversation from one patient to another, Messages asks which message is the new patient's first, with their name: for example Which is the first message that's Sam Example's? It lists the conversation's last 20 messages, newest first, and the newest is chosen. That is usually the message that made you move it.

  • Billing, providers and anyone tagged on the new patient see the message you pick and everything after it. Everything before it stays hidden from them, with a line saying so. You see everything.
  • The last choice, All of them (this conversation was always Sam Example's), gives them the whole conversation. Use it when the link was simply wrong from the start. Messages older than the 20 listed go to the new patient only this way.
  • Replies and notes staff wrote for the first patient stay with that patient, whatever you pick.

Linking a conversation from Needs matching for the first time, and Not a patient, ask nothing. Neither do moves Messages makes on its own.

A reply scheduled for 8:00 AM

A text sent during quiet hours can be scheduled for 8:00 AM. If one is waiting for the patient the conversation is leaving, moving it asks first: A reply is scheduled to this number at 8:00 AM. Cancel it? You never see its words here, only when it goes. Cancel it is chosen; press Continue.

  • Cancel sent, not confirmed: for now this is what you'll see. Spruce answers, but Messages can't yet be sure Spruce's cancel works, so the card says Cancel not confirmed, with Cancel sent to Spruce when this conversation moved, but not confirmed. Check Spruce to be sure the 8:00 AM reply didn't go out. Open the conversation in the Spruce app and check that the scheduled text is gone, before 8:00 AM.
  • Cancelled: once Spruce's cancel is confirmed to work, the reply's card says Cancelled, with A reply scheduled for 8:00 AM was cancelled because this conversation moved. Nothing is sent.
  • Spruce couldn't cancel it: the card says Couldn't cancel the 8:00 AM reply. Cancel it in Spruce. Do that in the Spruce app right away, before 8:00 AM.
  • Spruce had nothing left to cancel: Spruce had no 8:00 AM reply left to cancel. It may have gone out already. Check the conversation in Spruce.
  • Keep it: it goes out at 8:00 AM as written. The card says Kept when this conversation moved: it goes out at 8:00 AM.
  • Too close to 8:00 AM: within two minutes of its time Messages doesn't ask Spruce, because it may already be going. The card says Too close to 8:00 AM to cancel: it may have gone out. Check Spruce. Check the conversation in the Spruce app.
  • Several waiting: Messages cancels up to three right away and the rest within a minute or two; the message after the move says how many are being cancelled in the background, and each card shows Cancelling… until it's done.

The same question comes up when Link one message at a time undoes a link with such a reply waiting, and when you press Undo under a message linked on its own that has a reply scheduled from it (its card then says the reply was cancelled, or kept, because its message was unlinked from the patient). When Messages moves a conversation on its own (its number changed in Healthie: it is on another patient's chart, on none, or on two), it cancels these replies without asking, and the card says so. A reply you chose to keep stays kept: Messages never cancels it later on its own.

Faxes and shared contacts: one message at a time

Some conversations can't belong to one patient as a whole, so each message in them is linked on its own:

  • Faxes. A fax line brings faxes about many patients.
  • Shared numbers and addresses. One number or address reaches more than one patient: a parent texting about two children, a pharmacy, a number Healthie lists on two charts. Messages undoes any whole link made with it, yours included, and suggests that patient first.
  • More than five people on one email.

These show in Needs matching with Fax: link each one, Shared number, Shared address or Link each message, and how many of their messages are linked so far. Open one: the panel says why (Fax line, Shared number, Shared address), and every message has its own Link to patient under it. Press it, pick the patient (the one a link that was undone named comes first), and press Link. The page says Message linked. It shows in that patient's timeline.

For an email, the picker adds: Link it to the patient it is about. Billing and providers see only that it is there until you show it to them.

On an email with several addresses, Link one message at a time marks every address that has written in it, another parent, a school or a pharmacy included.

Only that message goes to the patient. It shows in their timeline, counts toward their Waiting and unread, and is archived with them; the rest of the conversation stays here. A provider or Billing sees it only if they handle that patient. Under a linked message, Undo takes it back here (if the patient hadn't dealt with it, the conversation waits on it again). If a teammate linked it meanwhile, yours is refused: Someone changed this message's patient meanwhile. Reload it and try again.

Marking a number or address shared yourself

When a "Which patient?" conversation is from a number or address more than one patient uses that Healthie doesn't know about (a pharmacy, a parent's phone on one child's chart), press Link one message at a time in its panel and confirm. Every whole link on that number or address is undone (links staff made are kept as the hint), and its messages are then linked one at a time.

On an email with several addresses, every address is marked. If marking stopped part way (a connection dropped), Link one message at a time is still offered: press it again, and it marks the addresses left.

If that was a mistake, Not shared after all takes it back, and the links it undid come back, on every address at once. Messages already linked on their own stay where they are, and the conversation keeps being linked one message at a time until you undo them. A share Messages made itself (a number on two charts in Healthie, or an address two patients' links collided on) can't be taken back here: fix the number in Healthie.

Junk faxes and other messages nobody needs

A fax nobody needs (an advert, a misdial) leaves Needs matching when you archive its conversation:

  1. Link any fax in it that belongs to a patient first, as above.
  2. In Needs matching, point at the fax line's row and press Archive (or open it and press Archive at the top).
  3. The row leaves Needs matching. Faxes already linked to a patient stay on that patient's timeline as they were: archiving the fax line never touches them.
  4. The next fax brings the fax line back to Needs matching, so nothing new goes unseen.

The same works for a shared number or address whose remaining messages need nothing.

Replying

From the patient's timeline you can reply to a message linked on its own. The reply goes to the shared number or address, and the composer says so: Shared number: more than one patient may read texts sent here. The reply is kept on that patient's timeline only. Messages linked on their own don't take internal notes; add the note on one of the patient's own conversations.

Chapter 08 of 16 · Routing

Mixed conversations

Family numbers, shared addresses and fax lines: what is hidden from Billing and providers, and why.

What a mixed conversation is

Most conversations belong to one patient. Some carry messages about more than one:

  • A family number or address. A parent texts or emails about two children who are both patients.
  • A pharmacy, a school or another office that writes about several patients from one number or address.
  • A fax line. Faxes about many patients arrive from one sender.
  • An email with more than five people on it.

Messages never links these to one patient as a whole. Each message is linked on its own to the patient it is about, and the conversation itself stays in Needs matching. How to link them is in Needs matching.

How Messages knows a contact is shared

  • A phone number is marked shared on its own when Healthie lists it on two or more charts.
  • An email address is marked shared when front desk marks it (Link one message at a time), or when its messages end up linked to two different patients.
  • A fax line and an email with more than five people are always linked one message at a time.

Until a number or address is marked shared, everything from it goes to the patient it is linked to. See "What Messages can't catch" below.

What is hidden, and from whom

Front desk and admins see the whole shared conversation in Needs matching, so nothing is hidden from them. Billing, providers and anyone tagged on a patient see only the messages linked to their patient. From an email they see only that it is there: who it is from and when. Its text, subject and attachments stay hidden until front desk reads it and shows it to them (below). Messages doesn't try to tell a writer's own words from what an email quotes: email apps quote in too many ways to tell reliably. The examples use invented patients, Sam and Alex, two brothers whose mother writes from one address.

What happens What a provider or Billing sees on Sam's timeline Why
Mom writes a new email about Sam's fever. Front desk links it to Sam. That there is an email from Mom, and when, with Only front desk can see this email’s text. They can show it to you if you need it. Its text, subject and attachments are hidden until front desk shows it to the team. Messages can't prove nothing in it comes from another email, so it never guesses.
Mom emailed about Alex's refill. Later she replies about Sam's fever, quoting the refill email. Front desk links the reply to Sam. The same: that there is an email from Mom, and when. The quoted part is about Alex.
That reply's subject is "Re: Alex refill". Subject hidden. A reply takes its subject from the thread, which can be about the other child.
Either email has attachments. None, until front desk shows the email to the team. A file may belong to the other child.
Front desk reads Mom's new email, sees it is all about Sam, and presses Show its text to the patient's team. The whole email: its text, subject and attachments. Front desk read it and decided.
A reply a provider or Billing sent from this timeline. The reply's text, without its subject. Messages knows it holds only what staff typed.
A new email front desk sent Sam's family from Messages. Its text and its subject. Staff wrote both, for Sam.
The other messages in the conversation, linked to Alex or not linked yet. Nothing. They don't appear on Sam's timeline at all. Only the message linked to Sam is Sam's.
The link that opens the conversation in the Spruce app. No link. It would open the whole conversation, outside these rules.

Front desk and admins read every email whole, where it is, subject and attachments included. Under one the team gets only in part they see Billing and providers who see this patient see only that this email is here. with Show its text to the patient's team. The hidden text never reaches anyone else unless front desk shows it to them (below): it isn't sent to their browser at all. Replies staff send from Messages show to everyone, since Messages knows they hold only what staff typed.

Texts, calls, voicemails and faxes have no quoted part, so each one shows whole to whoever handles the patient it is linked to.

Showing a hidden email to the patient's team

Front desk can read such an email and decide it is all about this patient. Then, under it, press Show its text to the patient's team. Messages asks first: Billing and providers who see this patient will see this whole email, including anything it quotes. Read it first. Press Show it to the team.

  • Billing, providers and anyone tagged on the patient then see that one email as you do: its text, subject and attachments, everywhere Messages shows it (the timeline, the list, search, Save to chart and forwarding). They see no hidden line on it.
  • Under the email you see Shown to the patient's team by (who), with the date, and Hide it again, which hides it from them as before. If Messages couldn't hide it just then, it says This email couldn’t be hidden just now. Nothing changed; try again. with Try again.
  • If someone forwards it while you hide it and show it again, their forward isn't sent: Front desk showed more of this email to the team since you opened it. Nothing was sent. Open it again and check what you forward.
  • It covers that one email only, for this patient only. If the message or its conversation is later linked to someone else, or the link is undone, it is hidden from the team again.
  • It never makes another patient's message this patient's. An email that belongs to someone else can't be shown here.

Show it only when all of it is about this patient. If part of it is about someone else (a quoted email about the other child), leave it hidden and pass on what matters yourself.

A conversation that moved to another patient

When front desk moves a whole conversation from one patient to another, they pick the first message that's the new patient's (see Needs matching). The new patient's Billing person, providers and anyone tagged see that message and everything after it; earlier messages stay hidden from them, with a line saying so. Each email after that point is shown to them the same way: that it is there, from whom and when, until front desk shows it to the patient's team. Front desk sees a line under each such email: Billing and providers who see this patient see only that this email is here. While such an email is hidden, a reply to it from Billing or a provider goes only to whoever sent it; once front desk shows it to the patient's team, they can add someone, as front desk can.

Replying and forwarding from a single message

  • A reply goes in the same thread, to the same people. If you're in Billing, a provider or tagged, you can reply only to people already on that email, and while its text is hidden from you only to whoever sent it: This email is linked to this patient on its own, so a reply goes only to people already on it. That way nobody new receives what was hidden from you. If you can't see who an email went to and there is nobody to reply to (an email the practice sent), the box says You can’t see whom this email went to, so you can’t reply to it here. Ask front desk to reply. Front desk can add someone.
  • A forward from Billing, a provider or someone tagged sends only what their timeline shows: a hidden text stays out (the forward says so), its attachments and whom it went to too, and a hidden subject becomes Fwd: message. Front desk and admins forward the whole email.
  • Notes can't be added to a message linked on its own yet. Add them to the patient another way for now.

What Messages can't catch

  • An address nobody has marked shared yet. Everything from it goes to the patient it is linked to, the other child's news included. Mark it shared as soon as you notice two patients behind one address.
  • One message about two patients. "Both boys need refills" can only be linked to one of them. Link it to the patient it's mostly about. The other patient's part has to be handled outside Messages for now.
  • What a text or fax says. Messages hides quoted email, not words. A text or fax that mentions another patient shows whole on the timeline of the patient it's linked to.

What front desk should do

  1. When two patients write from one number or address, press Link one message at a time on that conversation.
  2. Link each message to the patient it is about. Read an email first if you're not sure.
  3. Billing and providers see no email's text in these conversations. If they need one, read it yourself. When all of it is about their patient, press Show its text to the patient's team; otherwise pass on only what is about their patient.
  4. For a message about two patients, link it to the one it's mostly about.

Why it works this way

The rule: anyone who sees a patient but not the whole shared conversation (Billing, providers, anyone tagged) never gets words from a message that is someone else's. Front desk and admins see the whole conversation anyway, so hiding from them would protect nothing. Messages never shows Billing and providers an email's words here unless front desk read it and showed it to them.

The other ways we considered:

  • Show every linked message whole. Simplest, but a reply quoting a sibling's email would show the sibling's details to the wrong provider.
  • Hide every email from a shared address from Billing and providers, with no way to show one. Safest, but they'd lose the messages they need about their own patient. Front desk's Show its text to the patient's team is what makes hiding workable.
  • Split emails by the names in them. Names aren't reliable (nicknames, siblings with similar details), so it would be wrong both ways.
  • Find quotes by comparing with earlier emails in the thread. The quoted email may not be in a thread Messages can read (another thread or mailbox), so a comparison can't prove nothing is quoted.
  • Cut a reply where its quote starts, and show the part above. Messages did this first, using the marks Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook put on quotes. A review found email apps that mark quotes in other ways (a header block in another language, a quote inside a quote, an email attached to an email), and each time the earlier email showed. Adding marks one by one never ends, so Messages no longer cuts.
  • Release an email when it looks like the writer's own. Messages did this, in three rounds of rules (cutting at quote marks, then holding anything that looked like a quote, then releasing only plain-looking email). Each review found an email app's quoting that got through, so on November 23, 2026 Andy decided Messages stops guessing.

Decided November 22, 2026; cutting dropped November 23, 2026 after the second review. Showing a hidden email to the patient's team, and picking where a moved conversation's new patient starts, decided by Andy on November 23, 2026; that Messages shows no email automatically, decided by Andy on November 23, 2026. If the approach changes, this chapter changes with it, along with The patient timeline, Replying and notes and Billing and providers.

Chapter 09 of 16 · Routing

Handled by and hand-offs

Handing a patient to Billing or a provider, hand-backs, and the Slack alert.

Who handles a patient

Every patient has one owner: Front desk (the default), Billing as a team, or one person by name. Front desk and admins see the Handled by band under the patient card, with Front desk sees every patient. Billing and providers see the ones handed to them.

When people are tagged on the patient, the band also says Tagged: and their names, newest first. Hover over a name to see who tagged them and when. A name leaves the line when that person presses Clear. Being tagged doesn't make someone the owner: Handled by stays as it is.

The Handled by menu offers Front desk, Billing, staff who see every patient, and providers who are set up in Messages. Billing staff aren't offered by name, because Billing works as a team: hand to Billing instead.

Handing a patient off

Choose someone other than Front desk. A box opens, Hand to and their name, with room for a note: They see it with the patient, even if they cannot see the email. Press Hand off.

If someone else changes who handles the patient while the box is open, Messages doesn't replace their choice on that click. The box says who has the patient now, and the button becomes Hand off anyway: press it only if you still mean to. If Messages says This patient kept changing. Try again., nothing changed; the box stays open, so press Hand off again.

What happens next:

  • the note shows at the top of the patient's timeline and as a Handoff card;
  • Billing or the provider sees the patient on their list, waiting for them, until they archive it or hand it back;
  • the person it was handed to gets a Slack message, if they're set up for alerts (see below);
  • front desk still sees the patient too.

Handing a patient to a staff member by name (someone who sees every patient anyway) doesn't put it on a separate list. Their initials show on the row and the patient falls under their Mine.

Use the note for what they need to do. Don't put more patient detail in it than the job needs. Choosing Front desk takes the patient back at once, with no note.

Hand-backs

Billing and providers send a patient back with Hand back, and the note is required. The patient returns to front desk's list as waiting, with a violet banner: Handed back to front desk by the person, with waiting for staff and their note.

Hand back archives the conversations as they were when you opened the box. If new messages arrive, or someone changes who handles the patient, while it's open, the box says so and the first press doesn't send; Hand back anyway does. New messages stay open for front desk.

That wait clears when front desk:

  • replies from Messages to someone who wrote in, or sends a text from Messages;
  • archives the patient;
  • chooses who handles the patient.

A reply sent straight from Gmail, a forward or an internal note doesn't clear it. Archive the patient when you've dealt with it.

The Slack alert

When front desk or an admin hands a patient to someone by name, a provider or a staff member, that person gets a Slack direct message like this:

Synthetic Front Desk handed you a patient in Messages, with a note for you. (a link that opens the patient in Messages)

It says who handed the patient over and whether there's a note, and links to the patient. It never includes the patient's name, the note or anything from their messages. Opening the link asks them to sign in and checks they can see the patient.

There's no alert when:

  • the patient is handed to Billing or Front desk;
  • you hand a patient to yourself;
  • the patient was already waiting on their list and you added no note;
  • the person can't open Messages yet, or an admin hasn't linked their login to them and added their Slack ID (see Setting up Slack alerts and calls).

If they archived the patient and you hand the patient to them again, they're alerted again.

Chapter 10 of 16 · Routing

Save to chart

Putting an attachment in the patient's Healthie documents, staff only.

Saving a file to the chart

Staff can put an attachment straight into the patient's Documents in Healthie. Next to each file in a patient's timeline (email attachments, Spruce files and voicemail recordings) is a small document icon, Save to chart. Providers don't have it.

A fax saves to the chart once it is linked to that patient on its own (see Needs matching): open the patient and use Save to chart on it, as on any file. A fax not linked yet can't be saved from Messages. On an email linked on its own, Billing can save its attachments only once front desk has shown the email to the patient's team; until then they stay with front desk.

The box says Save the file to the patient's documents in Healthie. Staff only: the patient will not see it. Press Save to chart.

  • The file lands in the patient's Documents, staff only, named after the file, with Saved from Messages by your name.
  • The limit is 10 MB a file. A bigger one says This file is too large to save from here. Add it in Healthie instead.
  • The same file is only ever saved once to the same patient: Already in the patient's chart.
  • If the conversation stopped being this patient's while you had it open, the save is refused. Reload and try again.

When a save isn't confirmed

Healthie sometimes takes too long to answer. Then the page says We couldn’t confirm it was saved. Look in the patient’s documents in Healthie before saving again. Messages never saves it again on its own.

Under the timeline, a reminder lists the file: We couldn’t confirm the file was saved to this patient’s chart. The patient stays in front desk's Inbox with a Chart save to check chip until someone checks.

  1. Open the patient's Documents in Healthie.
  2. If the file is there, press I’ve checked, dismiss.
  3. If it isn't, press Save to chart on the file again. The box now asks you to check first; press It’s not there, save again.

The reminder also appears when a file was saved but its conversation moved to another patient during the save. Check in Healthie that it belongs on this chart.

Chapter 11 of 16 · Billing and providers

If you're in Billing or a provider

Your list, handing a patient back, and what you can and can't do.

Your list

If you're in Billing or a provider, your list holds only the patients front desk handed to you. A banner says so at the top:

  • Billing: You see only patients handed to Billing, and patients you're tagged on.
  • Providers: You see only patients handed to you, and patients you're tagged on, and, without email access, Email stays with front desk and billing.

You don't have Needs matching or the Handled by menu; front desk does the matching and routing. You never see conversations that aren't linked to a patient.

Providers see only Messages and their own Settings (Account and Appearance) in the sidebar, and the dashboard opens straight on Messages. There's no patient search box at the top for providers.

A patient stays on your list while there's something there for you: a conversation you can see, a hand-off note, or a hand-off still waiting for you.

Working a patient

Open the patient. A violet banner shows who handed them over and their note, with waiting for you.

You can:

  • read the conversations you have access to;
  • reply by text, and by email if you have email access (Billing always does);
  • write internal notes for the team;
  • open and download attachments;
  • send a new email, with email access;
  • call the patient from your own phone with Call (see Calling a patient), once an admin has added your phone.

Providers don't have Details (the full patient record from Healthie) or Save to chart. Open chart is there for everyone.

A message from a shared number or address shows only if front desk linked it to your patient, and only that message. From an email you see who it is from and when; its text, subject and attachments stay hidden until front desk shows it to you, since an email can quote another patient's. It says Only front desk can see this email’s text. They can show it to you if you need it. Ask front desk if you need it. The same holds for emails in a conversation that moved to your patient. See Mixed conversations.

Finishing: Archive or Hand back

When you've dealt with it, you have two choices.

  • Archive closes the conversations you can see. The patient stays yours and comes back on your list when something new arrives.
  • Hand back returns the patient to front desk. Write what front desk needs to do; the note is required. The conversations you can see are archived in the same step, as they were when you opened the box, and front desk sees the patient as waiting, with your note on top. Anything new that arrives while the box is open stays open for front desk, and the box tells you before you confirm.

The page says Handed back to front desk, and the patient leaves your list.

You can also archive your own patients from the list without opening them, one at a time or several selected together. See Archiving from the list.

When you're tagged

Front desk or an admin can tag you in an internal note to ask you to look at a patient (see Tagging a teammate). That patient then shows on your list with a Tagged chip, even if it isn't handed to you. Hover over the chip to see who tagged you and when. The Tagged filter lists the patients you're tagged on; it shows once someone has tagged you.

Open the patient. A blue banner stays at the top of the patient's page, under their name, even as you scroll. It says who tagged you and when, with their note and Clear. A long note shows two lines; Show all opens the rest.

When you're there only because of the tag, you can read the conversations you have access to, reply, write notes and call. Archive, Hand back, Send and archive, Forward, new emails and Save to chart aren't offered: whoever handles the patient does those. Without email access you see the note, but not the email. If the patient is handed to someone else while you have it open, and you're still tagged, the page switches to this at once: the hand-off notes and the buttons above go, and the page reloads the patient.

An email reply goes only to people already in the conversation. To and Cc start with them; you can remove someone, but not add a new address. The composer says You were tagged on this patient, so you can reply only to people already in this conversation. To bring someone else in, ask whoever handles the patient.

When you've done what was asked, press Clear. The page says Tag cleared, and a patient you had only because of the tag leaves your list. A patient that's also handed to you stays. If someone tagged you again since you opened the patient, Clear asks you to read the new note first.

Slack alerts (providers)

If an admin has linked your dashboard login to you on the Users page, and your entry on the People page has your Slack ID, you get a Slack message when front desk hands you a patient. Billing gets no Slack alert, because patients go to Billing as a team. It says who handed it over and links to the patient. It never names the patient or repeats the note, so open the link to see what's needed.

You get the same kind of Slack message when someone tags you: who tagged you, and the link.

Chapter 12 of 16 · For admins

Settings › Inboxes

Connecting Gmail mailboxes, choosing which Spruce lines show in Messages, and Archive in Spruce and Gmail.

The Inboxes page

Settings › Inboxes lists the Gmail mailboxes and Spruce lines that feed Messages. Only admins can change them; everyone else sees Only admins can connect mailboxes or change Spruce lines.

Gmail mailboxes

Each mailbox shows a badge:

  • Connected, with who connected it, when it last synced, and whether new mail shows up within seconds or within a minute.
  • Needs reconnect: Google access was lost, so mail is not syncing and its conversations are hidden from Messages. Connect it again below.
  • Disconnected, with the date and Its conversations are hidden from Messages.

While a mailbox is Needs reconnect or Disconnected, all of its conversations disappear from Messages: rows, patient timelines, counts and the From choices for new email. They come back when it's reconnected. Messages says so at the top for a mailbox that needs reconnecting: A mailbox needs reconnecting in Settings › Inboxes. Its email is hidden here until then.

Connecting a mailbox

  1. Type the mailbox address in Mailbox. It must be a @threeriversmentalhealth.com address.
  2. Press Connect.
  3. Google asks you to sign in. Sign in as this mailbox itself, not your own account, and click Allow. Leave the Gmail box checked.
  4. You come back to the page with the mailbox Connected.

If you sign in as a different account, nothing is saved: Signed in to Google as a different account than the mailbox. Start again and sign in as the mailbox.

The first sync brings in the last 14 days of mail, at most 300 messages, as history. History never reopens anything already archived. The conversations it brings in show as open and unread, and one whose last message from outside was never answered shows as Waiting until someone replies or archives it. Expect some catching up after connecting a mailbox.

If a mailbox couldn't sync for a long while (Gmail keeps its change history about a week), Messages catches up on everything since its last good sync, up to a couple of hundred emails a minute, while new mail keeps arriving as usual. Until it's done, the mailbox here says Catching up on missed mail with the dates still being brought in, and the status at the top of Messages says the mailbox is catching up on missed mail. Missed mail comes in as new mail, however old: an email nobody answered opens its conversation and shows as Waiting from when it was sent; one that a later reply already answered shows, unread, without opening anything.

Disconnecting

Disconnect asks first. Messages stops reading and sending from that mailbox, and Google removes its access. Nothing in the mailbox itself changes. Connecting again needs a new sign-in as the mailbox.

Spruce lines

Texts, calls, voicemails and faxes on the lines turned on here show in Messages. Turning a line off hides its conversations there, patient timelines included; turning it back on brings them back, with its last 3 days. Spruce stays as it is. Each line has a switch.

  • Turning a line on: its conversations start showing in Messages, and the last 3 days come in once, as history, shortly after. As with a new mailbox, these show as open and unread, and unanswered ones as Waiting.
  • Turning a line off: its conversations disappear from Messages within seconds, patient timelines included, and nobody can send on it from Messages. Nothing changes in Spruce. Turn it back on and its last 3 days come in again.

The footer says how quickly new messages arrive and when Messages last checked Spruce.

Calls go out from

Calls go out from picks the line patients see when someone presses Call in Messages. Only phone lines that are on are listed. No calls from Messages stops calls: pressing Call then says calls aren't set up. If the chosen line is switched off above, calls stop until you choose another line or turn it back on.

Archive in Spruce and Gmail

Archive in Spruce and Gmail decides whether Archive in Messages follows into Spruce and Gmail, and whether archiving there follows back here. It starts Off. Choose one:

  • Off: Archive stays in Messages only. Spruce and Gmail are left as they are.
  • Watch only: for the test conversations listed below it, Messages notes what Spruce and Gmail do and changes nothing anywhere. Use it to see how a test conversation behaves before anything changes.
  • Test: for the test conversations only, Archive and Move to Inbox follow into Spruce and Gmail, and archiving there follows back here.
  • On: the same for every conversation on the Spruce lines and Gmail mailboxes above. It asks first.

In Gmail, archiving only takes the thread out of the inbox; nothing is deleted. Conversations archived before you turn it on stay as they are, here and there.

Test conversations takes one entry per line: patient: and a Healthie patient ID (all of that patient's conversations), spruce: and a Spruce conversation ID, or gmail: and a mailbox, a slash and a Gmail thread ID. Save test conversations saves the list; if an entry isn't one of those, the page says so and saves nothing.

When Spruce or Gmail doesn't follow, the conversation says so in Messages (see Chips about Spruce and Gmail). Turning it back to Off stops it at once; anything still waiting to go to Spruce or Gmail is dropped.

Chapter 13 of 16 · For admins

Settings › Messages access

The staff switch, each person's team and extras, what the extras really do, and who each login is.

The Messages access page

Settings › Messages access decides who sees what. Roles (admin, staff, provider) come from each person's dashboard account and aren't changed here. Here you choose each person's team and anything extra they cover. Only admins can change it.

Staff can use Messages

The switch at the top, Staff can use Messages, opens Messages to everyone who is set up. Admins always can. Turn it on once the practice mailbox is connected and people are set up. Turning it off hides Messages from staff right away. It covers providers too, even though it says staff.

While it's off, the page shows Messages is open only to admins until staff access is turned on above. You can set people up first. Each row still says what that person will see once it's on, so you can check a setup before turning it on.

Setting someone up

The list shows every enabled dashboard user with their role badge (Admin, Staff, Provider or No role) and a sentence saying what they see. Not set up yet means they have no Messages setup. Admin and No role rows can't be edited.

For staff:

  • Team: Front desk or Billing.
  • Also sees: Front desk inbox, for Billing staff only. Front desk staff already see every patient and their email, so they're offered no extras.

For providers:

  • Also sees: Billing and Email. Providers have no team and can't cover the front desk inbox; someone who covers the front desk needs a staff account.

Press Set up for someone new (staff start on Front desk), or Save after a change. The change reaches their open dashboard within a minute.

What each extra does

  • Front desk inbox makes a Billing staff member work as front desk: every patient, Needs matching and Handled by, and no Hand back.
  • Billing, for a provider, adds the patients handed to Billing.
  • Email, for a provider, shows email. Without it, a provider sees only texts, calls, voicemails and notes.

The page only offers an extra where it changes something.

Who each login is

Under each person, a line says who their login is on the People page and whether Slack messages and Call work for them, for example Linked to a name, Slack messages: on. Call: off, no mobile on People. Nothing here can be changed: logins are linked to people on the Users page, and each person's Slack ID and mobile are on People (see Setting up Slack alerts and calls).

Not linked: no Slack messages or Call. Link them on Users. means the login isn't linked to anyone, so that person gets no Slack messages from Messages and can't use Call, and Messages shows the login's own name.

Your own row has a You badge, so you can tell which login you're signed in with.

If someone else changed it

If the same person was saved somewhere else while you were editing (by another admin, or by you in another tab), the page says their access was changed somewhere else while you were editing, shows what it now reads, and offers Start over from theirs. Your own save never counts as a change made elsewhere.

Chapter 14 of 16 · For admins

Setting up Slack alerts and calls

Slack IDs and mobiles on People, and linking each dashboard login to its person on Users.

What Slack alerts and calls need

When front desk or an admin hands a patient to someone in Messages, or tags them in a note, that person gets a Slack direct message with a link to the patient (see Handled by and hand-offs). It goes through the same Slack messages providers already get for appointments and unsigned notes. Call in Messages rings the caller's own mobile.

Both work the same way: Messages follows the person's dashboard login to who they are in Healthie, on the People page. That person's entry holds their Slack ID and their mobile. It works for providers and staff alike.

Adding someone's Slack ID and mobile

  1. Open People in the sidebar. Providers and Staff at the top narrow the list.
  2. Press the pencil next to the person.
  3. Fill in Slack User ID and Mobile. The same mobile gets credential reminder texts and is the phone they dial from when they press Call. Turn Active off for someone who has left: they get no Slack messages from Messages and can't use Call.
  4. Press Save.

Each person needs their own Slack ID and their own mobile. If someone else already has the one you typed, the dialog says is already on that person and Save stays off.

Only admins see full mobile numbers. Everyone else sees the last four digits.

Linking a login to a person

  1. Open Users in the sidebar (under Settings).
  2. Choose Edit user from the menu at the end of the login's row. When you invite someone new, the same field is in Invite user.
  3. Under This login is, pick the person. If someone in Healthie has the same email as the login, a link under the field offers them, ending the same email in Healthie.
  4. Press Save changes.

The Person column on Users and the Dashboard Login column on People show the link. Messages shows that person's name for the login from then on. A login can be linked to one person, and a person to one login. Picking a different person for a login moves the link. A person already linked to another login isn't offered until that login is unlinked, disabled or deleted. If someone has left Healthie, the Person column says no longer in Healthie; choose Not linked to anyone in Edit user to clear it.

Linking a login doesn't change its role. A provider's login shows its role as Provider, and it can't be changed on this page.

Not linked to anyone is right for logins that aren't anyone in Healthie, such as a test login. They get no Slack messages and can't use Call.

Checking it worked

Open Settings › Messages access. Each person's line says who their login is linked to, and whether Slack messages and Call are on. If one is off, the line says why: no Slack ID or mobile on People, or someone else has the same one.

When an alert doesn't arrive

  • The person can't use Messages yet. Check Staff can use Messages and their setup in Settings › Messages access.
  • Their login isn't linked to them on Users, or their entry on People has no Slack ID.
  • Someone else on People has the same Slack ID.
  • They're marked inactive on People.
  • They already had the patient waiting on their list, and the hand-off had no note.

Alerts never hold up the hand-off: if Slack is slow or down, the patient is still handed over. A new link or Slack ID can take a few minutes to start working.
